key_insight: Routing codes are a new family of qLDPC codes that keep high encoding rates while making non-local connections shorter, sparser, and fully parallel.
engineering_relevance: They are designed for practical quantum hardware because they reduce wiring complexity on superconductors and simplify atom-movement scheduling in neutral-atom systems.
method: Construct a qLDPC family called routing codes.
Optimize code structure to lower connectivity and shorten non-local couplings.
Make all non-local couplings mutually parallel to avoid crossings and simplify implementation.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations show weight-7 routing codes can cut physical qubit overhead by about 8× versus surface codes at the same logical error rate.
watch_item: The abstract reports promising simulation results, but real hardware performance will still depend on fabrication constraints, control errors, and scaling the routing architecture.
paper_title: Routing Codes: High-Rate Quantum LDPC Codes with Short, Parallel Non-Local Connectivity
